note: 'How many Finance Commissions have submitted reports so far?' (keyed: Twelve). Not taught: the count is time-bound and changes with every five-year cycle; the chapter teaches the Article 280 cycle and composition, and no fetched source used for this chapter states a running count of commissions.
Taught: the Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members, all appointed by the President (Art 280(1), claim c19); also an exam_note box in the section.

Partly covered only: this chapter teaches that Finance Commission recommendations (Art 281, c24) and CAG reports (Art 151, c30) are laid before Parliament by the President, and the CAG section's deep text uses this very chain. But the keyed answer also requires the National Commission for Scheduled Castes report (Art 338), which belongs to POL-19, so the full key is not derivable from this chapter alone.

Not taught: the Public Accounts Committee's size, remit and working belong to POL-10 (parliamentary procedure). Only statement 3 (PAC examines the CAG's report) touches this chapter's subject; the chapter does not teach PAC composition or functions.
Taught: Article 280 lays down the Finance Commission (claim c19); the section's exam_note box names this exact article-body pairing.
Taught: members of a State Public Service Commission are appointed by the Governor of the State (Art 316(1), claim c04).
Not taught: the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee being from the Opposition is a parliamentary-committee convention belonging to POL-10; this chapter covers the CAG, not the PAC.

Not taught: 'a Public Service Commission was first established by the Government of India Act, 1919' is pre-constitutional legislative history (HIS-27 scope). This chapter teaches only the constitutional scheme of Articles 315-323; none of the sources fetched for it covers the 1919 Act.

Taught: the Finance Commission is a constitutional body because Article 280 itself creates it (claim c19), and the section's dont_confuse box teaches the constitutional-vs-statutory distinction the question tests. The National Commission for Women limb (a statutory body) is POL-19's subject in detail.
Taught: the Attorney General for India is appointed by the President (Art 76(1), claim c32); the section's standard text names this exact exam point.
